classification.difficultyReason: Infer the cylindrical length from the overall length, then combine cylinder and sphere formulas while excluding internal joins.

content.prompt:
A storage tank is constructed as a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end of the cylinder. The radius of the cylinder is 1.5 m and the overall length of the tank is 6 m.

Calculate:

spec.description: Upright cylinder with hemispherical ends and elliptical circular joins; no measurement labels. Ordinary source blue outlines and red hidden arcs are rendered black, retaining dashed hidden arcs.
spec.mathematics: Two hemispheres of radius r form one sphere. Overall axial length equals cylindrical length plus 2r. Circular joins are internal surfaces.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry is supplied; no answers or inferred dimensions appear.

children.label: a
children.prompt: the surface area of the tank in $\mathrm{m}^2$

answer.worked:
The two hemispheres form one sphere. The cylindrical length is $6-2(1.5)=3\ \mathrm{m}$. Only the curved cylinder surface and the hemispherical surfaces are exposed.
$$\begin{align*}S&=2\pi rh+4\pi r^2\\S&=2\pi(1.5)(3)+4\pi(1.5)^2\\S&=9\pi+9\pi\\S&=18\pi\ \mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$

The cylindrical length is $6-2(1.5)=3\ \mathrm{m}$, and the two hemispheres form one sphere.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^2h+\frac43\pi r^3\\V&=\pi\left(\frac32\right)^2(3)+\frac43\pi\left(\frac32\right)^3\\V&=\frac{27\pi}{4}+\frac{18\pi}{4}\\V&=\frac{45\pi}{4}\ \mathrm{m}^3\end{align*}$$
